title: Performance sync — spotcheck retro and odd-latency scavenger hunt
content:
Purpose:
Quick sync notes from the 2026-10-11 Performance Spotcheck meeting. We ran a short scavenger-hunt-style investigation into several small regressions flagged by the daily QA sweep and a customer report of intermittent high tail latency. This doc captures observations, short experiments we ran, hypotheses, and next actions (fast experiments we can run in the next 48 hours).

Attendees:
- Riya Banerjee (owner)
- Diego Martinez (trace/observability)
- Asha Patel (batching/runtime)
- Liam Chen (KV cache/ops)
- Nora Kim (CI / throughput harness)

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- Symptom: p50 latency for mixed-short workloads drifted from ~18ms to ~30–45ms in the last 48h; p99 spikes up to 1.6–1.9s intermittently. Throughput (tokens/sec at steady state) down ~10–14% for mixed seq customers on dedicated nodes.
- Likely correlates: a) small increase in KV-cache miss-rate (observed from 11% -> 29% on affected pods), b) higher microburst-induced CPU steal observed on a subset of hosts, and c) a kernel driver update deployed two nights ago on the infra pool used by the nightly shadow runs.
- Immediate mitigation: pin the kernel module to the previous release in shadow environment and flip model fallback to a higher-LRU cache TTL for a small cohort.

What we observed (data snippets):
- Sample run (10/10 22:00 UTC) baseline vs current: p50: 18.2ms -> 34.7ms; p90: 120ms -> 240ms; p99: 480ms -> 1.7s. Throughput for 8xA10 pod: 650k tokens/min -> 560k tokens/min (steady state sampling).
- KV-cache: miss-rate baseline 11% -> 29% (measured by kv-cache metrics: cache.gets vs cache.misses) for the same traceIDs. Misses concentrated on sessions with interleaved short-context requests (chat-like).
- Warmup behavior: cold-start contribution unchanged. But we saw increased hop-counts in the batcher (more 1-item microbatches) under the same QPS, indicating the batching heuristic is fragmenting due to varying latencies per request.
- Host-level: on 3/24 affected machines we saw CPU steal spikes (1s granularity) correlated with elevated syscall latency. No OOMs or GPU timeouts.

Quick experiments run during the meeting (results):
1) Shadow pin: pinned kernel driver to previous build on a canary host -> p50 improved ~9ms and p99 tail dropped by ~200ms in 30min window.
2) Batcher TTL bump: increased batcher collection-window from 8ms -> 12ms in a canary run -> improved batching efficiency (7% fewer 1-item batches) and recovered ~4% throughput, but increased median by ~1.5ms due to slightly longer wait.
3) KV cache TTL increase (on canary route): TTL 300s -> 900s reduced observed miss-rate by ~8 percentage points for that route; apparent latency improvement for repeat-prefix sequences.
4) Kernel revert + batcher TTL combined: best short-term improvement (p50 ~ back to 19–21ms, throughput to -3% vs baseline).

Hypotheses (ranked):
H1 - KV-cache temperature shifted: some user/chat workloads are causing more session churn and evictions (recent routing changes made certain long-running sessions land on a smaller cache shard). This increases backend recomputation and stalls overall batching.
H2 - Kernel/driver change induced small scheduling jitter on affected host OSes causing syscall/backpressure on CPU-bound preparatory work, leading to more microbatches and divergence in latency distribution.
H3 - Recent micro-optimizations in nonblocking I/O changed ordering for a small fraction of requests, creating pathological interleaving with prefix cache checks and inflating tail latency.

Investigation plan (next 48–72 hours):
- Short-term (0–48h):
  * Action A: Roll kernel pin to the broader shadow pool for 24h observation. Owner: Diego. Due: 2026-10-13. Linked: JIRA-INF-2024.
  * Action B: Deploy batcher TTL experiment to 5% of traffic on dedicated staging to quantify throughput/latency trade-off. Owner: Asha. Due: 2026-10-13.
  * Action C: Increase KV-cache shard size for two suspect routes and enable per-route cache metrics tracing (trace ID tagging). Owner: Liam. Due: 2026-10-14.
- Medium-term (48–72h):
  * Action D: Run a synthetic mixed-sequence stress harness that reproduces the observed miss patterns (script: mixed_seq_synth_v2) and capture flamegraphs + syscall histograms. Owner: Nora. Due: 2026-10-15.
  * Action E: Reproduce the batching fragmentation locally with a deterministic replay of traces and validate whether the newer I/O change increases 1-item batches. Owner: Asha + Riya. Due: 2026-10-15.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Matrix rows: {kernel pinned | kernel same}, {batcher ttl 8/12/16ms}, {kv-cache ttl 300/900/3600s}, {shard count baseline / +2 / +4}.
- Primary metrics: p50, p90, p99, tokens/sec steady, kv-cache miss-rate, 1-item-batch-rate.
- Stop criteria: if p99 < 750ms and throughput >= -5% baseline for two consecutive 30m windows.

Notes about data fidelity / caveats:
- Our sampling cadence for the daily QA sweep uses 1m windows which can mute short microburst effects. We need high-resolution tracing (10–100ms bins) for the next runs.
- There is a confound: we saw a small rollout of routing-change R-892 last week that moved a fraction of traffic to a different cache shard keyspace. That rollout is partial and may explain the shard pressure. Liam to produce the exact traffic split map.
- The customer report mentioned >75% of affected requests followed a short prompt -> short response pattern (chat), which matches the mixed-seq traces.

Decisions made in-meeting:
- Do immediate kernel pin in shadow and expand to 10% shadow traffic if the canary maintains improvement for 2 hours. (Agreed)
- Do NOT roll kernel revert to prod yet — need synthetic reproduction and confirmation that this is the core cause. (Agreed)
- Run a short-lived batcher TTL 12ms on a staged cohort and measure user-facing error rates and cost delta before scaling.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Q1: Are any of the recent rollout commits to routing keys (R-892) composable with shard resizing? Could we transparently migrate hot sessions off smaller shards? (Owner: Liam)
- Q2: Is the kernel rollback masking a deeper scheduling bug in our userland code? What if the kernel pin only reduces but does not eliminate the problem under higher QPS? (Owner: Diego + Asha)
- Q3: Can we add quick telemetry to tag 1-item microbatches with cause (idle timeout vs early-evict) to make debugging easier? (Owner: Nora)

Action item summary (who / what / due):
- Diego: kernel pin to broader shadow pool, monitor 24h (Due 2026-10-13).
- Asha: batcher TTL 5% traffic experiment + local reproduction run (Due 2026-10-13 / 2026-10-15).
- Liam: expand cache shard tracing + report exact traffic split for R-892 (Due 2026-10-14).
- Nora: run synthetic mixed_seq_synth_v2 harness with flamegraphs and syscall histograms (Due 2026-10-15).
- Riya: coordinate findings, own the postmortem if regression confirmed, and draft a one-pager for CS to communicate to impacted customers (Due 2026-10-17).

Appendix: quick paste of command snippets used during the canary runs:
- Shadow kernel pin: /scripts/infra/pin-kernel.sh --pool shadow-canary --version 5.12.3-rev4
- Batcher TTL override (staging): curl -X POST $STAGING_API/routes/batcher-config -d '{"route":"chat-mixed","ttl_ms":12}'
- KV-shard trace: export KV_TRACE=1; curl -H "X-Trace-ID: synth-20261011-1" $SERVICE/embeddings?prompt=...

Notes to self: keep the next sync tight (30m) and bring only the owners and tracing people. If a synthetic run reproduces regressions, we should expand to a short maintenance window for a controlled kernel rollback on one dedicated cluster and run soak.

-- Riya
